I am a 40-year-old woman farming a small rented wheat plot of about a quarter-timad in Tigray. I will go to the cooperative to get some DAP and urea, but I know they may not have enough, so I will apply what I can afford and supplement it with manure from my homestead. I will sow my own saved seed because improved wheat seed is hard to find and too expensive for a rented plot this small. My family will do all the work—ploughing with our neighbor's oxen in exchange for labor, planting, weeding, and harvesting—because hiring workers would cost more than this little plot could return.
